transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've just been feeling tired all the time, and I haven't got any energy. It's been going on for a while now and I'm not managing as well as I used to.
Do you have any allergies or bad reactions to any medicines?
There's a painkiller that makes me terribly sick — I can't quite recall the name of it offhand.
How much is the tiredness affecting your usual day-to-day activities?
It's slowing me right down, to be honest. I've had to give up my swimming, and I'm not managing things around the house like I used to.
Could you tell me what medicines you're taking now, including any that have been started or changed recently, and the dose if you know it?
I take a few tablets each day — something for my diabetes, one for my thyroid, one for indigestion, and I buy some painkillers for my shoulder. I couldn't tell you the doses, sorry.
Have you ever had any operations or spent time in hospital?
No, I don't think I've ever had an operation or been in hospital for anything.
How bad would you say your tiredness is these days: mild, moderate, or severe, or are you not sure?
I'd say it's on the worse side — more than mild, that's for certain.
Along with the tiredness, have you noticed anything else that's changed in how you've been feeling?
I get more short of breath than I used to, especially going up hills, and a couple of friends have said I look a bit pale.
When you feel this tiredness, is it more in one part of your body, or does it feel like it's all over?
It's not in any one place — it's just a general sort of tiredness all over.
Is there anything you've noticed that seems to make your tiredness better or worse?
It tends to get worse as the day goes on — by the afternoon I'm really flagging.
When did you first start feeling this tiredness?
It's come on gradually — it's been creeping up on me for a while now.
What, if anything, worries you most about this tiredness?
I'm worried I won't be able to keep looking after my husband. He's got Parkinson's, and I do everything for him — if I keep feeling like this I don't know how I'll manage.
Have you noticed if your medicines make your tiredness better, worse, or make no difference, or are you not sure?
I really couldn't say — I've not noticed any difference one way or the other, to be honest.
Can you tell me what the tiredness actually feels like for you?
It's hard to describe — it's just a heavy, worn-out feeling, like I've got nothing left in the tank. It's there all day really.
Is there anything else about your past health problems that you'd like to add?
I've had diabetes for a fair few years now, and I've also got an underactive thyroid. Those are the main things I see the doctor about.
Is there anything else you've noticed about how you've been feeling that you'd like to add?
I sleep about seven hours, but I still wake up feeling unrefreshed. And I suppose my mood's been a bit flat with all the caring, if I'm honest.
Are you aware of any allergies or bad reactions to medicines, are there none that you know of, or are you not sure?
Yes, sorry — it's codeine. It makes me very sick if I take it.
Thinking about the tiredness and lack of energy, did that start suddenly, come on gradually, or are you not sure?
It came on gradually, over about two months or so.
Is there anything else about your health in the past that you'd like to add?
The diabetes has been going on for about twelve years now, so I'm fairly used to that. The thyroid trouble came along too, but I couldn't tell you exactly when.
Is there anything else you've noticed about how you've been feeling that you'd like to add?
I've not had any chest pain or lost any weight, and my bowels have been fine — nothing like that going on.
How bad would you say the tiredness is? Is it mild, moderate, or severe, or are you not sure?
I'd put my energy at about 3 out of 10, if that helps. It's a big change for me — I used to swim twice a week and I've had to stop that.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
